home.lede: Michael Meding is a German mining executive who has led the Los Azules copper project in San Juan, Argentina, since February 2022 and is Managing Director of McEwen Copper. Under his leadership the project received its environmental permit, published its feasibility study and became the first copper project approved under Argentina's RIGI investment regime. He was named Mining Entrepreneur of the Year in 2024 and 2025 and is president of GEMERA, Argentina's chamber of exploration companies.[[r:join,mux-bio,eia,fs,rigi-ln,fm-2024,fm-2025,gemera-ej]]

overview: Los Azules is the 10th largest undeveloped copper porphyry in the world by total mineral resources, high in the Andes of Calingasta, San Juan. Michael Meding took charge in February 2022, first as Vice President and General Manager and, since 2026, as Managing Director of McEwen Copper. In his first year the team grew from 32 to 142 direct employees, and over the three drilling seasons that led to the feasibility study it drilled more than 120,000 metres. In the same years he brought in Stellantis and Rio Tinto's Nuton as strategic investors, signed a collaboration agreement with the IFC and appointed Société Générale as financial advisor for project debt. The final investment decision is expected in mid-2027, with first commercial cathode targeted for 2030.[[r:fs,join,li-team,stellantis,nuton35,ifc,sg,loan-pr]]

He was born in Düsseldorf and finished school at the Alfred Krupp Schule in Essen, in the Ruhr, where his grandfather worked underground as a coal miner. He started at PwC, which sent him to Switzerland; he stayed seven years and joined Novartis through its CFO development programme. A move to Chile began more than fifteen years in Latin America, with CFO roles at multinational companies in Chile and Argentina. He came to mining in 2010 as CFO of Barrick Gold's Argentine operations, where he played a key role in the turnaround and mine life extension of Veladero and in the strategic partnership with Shandong Gold. At Trafigura he was CFAO of a polymetallic mining operation. He has worked in eight countries across Europe and the Americas and lives between San Juan and Toronto.[[r:li-abitur,li-ruhr,tsj2023,mp2014,mux-bio]]

He is president of GEMERA, the first foreigner to hold the role, vice president of CAEM and a member of the executive committee of the Cámara Minera de San Juan. He chaired Argentina Cobre, the country's copper conference, as honorary president in 2025 and president in 2026. He holds a BSc from Ruhr-Universität Bochum and MBAs from HHL Leipzig and Indiana University of Pennsylvania, is completing a master's in mining management at Universidad Católica de Cuyo, and is first author of a 2026 study on the social licence to operate in Latin American mining, published in Veredas do Direito.[[r:gemera-ej,handelsblatt,cmsj,li-cobre25,la-cobre26,veredas]]

home.la_brief: Los Azules is a copper porphyry in the Andes of Calingasta, San Juan. The October 2025 feasibility study designs an open pit, heap leach and SX-EW mine that would make 99.99% copper cathode at site, with no concentrate shipped, no tailings dam and 100% renewable power. Proven and probable reserves contain 10.2 billion pounds of copper (effective 3 September 2025) and support a 21-year mine life in the base case. It was the first copper project admitted to Argentina's RIGI. Resources, economics, financing and the growth case are on the Los Azules page.[[r:fs,ypf,rigi-ln]]

They include the final investment decision and full project financing expected in mid-2027, commercial cathode production targeted for 2030, the 2038 carbon-neutral goal, potential mine life extensions and the financing plan. They reflect McEwen Copper's current expectations, are not guarantees, and depend on financing, engineering, permits, metal prices, conditions in Argentina and the other risks described in McEwen Inc.'s filings with the SEC and on SEDAR+. Actual results may differ materially. Key assumptions, parameters and estimation methods are set out in the feasibility study announcement and the technical report.

faq.a: A copper porphyry project in the Andes of Calingasta, San Juan, owned by McEwen Copper. Its October 2025 feasibility study plans an open pit, heap leach and SX-EW operation producing 99.99% copper cathode at site, averaging 204,800 tonnes a year in its first five years.[[r:fs]]
In the department of Calingasta, San Juan province, at about 3,500 metres, roughly 80 km west-northwest of Calingasta and 6 km east of the Chilean border.[[r:mux-la]]
Michael Meding, Managing Director of McEwen Copper, has led the project since February 2022.[[r:join,mux-bio]]
McEwen Inc. 46.3%, Stellantis 18.2%, Nuton (a Rio Tinto venture) 17.2%, Rob McEwen 13.0%, Victor Smorgon Group 3.0% and other shareholders 2.3%.[[r:mux-la]]

faq.q: When will Los Azules produce copper?
faq.a: McEwen Copper expects a final investment decision and full project financing in mid-2027, and is targeting first commercial copper cathode in 2030.[[r:loan-pr]]

faq.q: Why is the Los Azules design different?
faq.a: The design would make finished copper cathode at the mine instead of concentrate, with no tailings dam, 100% renewable power, 74% less water than conventional milling and a carbon intensity of 1,082 kg CO2-e per tonne against an estimated industry average of 4,026.[[r:fs,ypf]]

faq.q: Is Los Azules approved under Argentina's RIGI?
faq.a: Yes. Resolución 1553/2025, published on 14 October 2025, admitted Los Azules with an investment plan of US$2,672 million. It was the first copper project approved under the regime.[[r:rigi-bo,rigi-ln]]

The feasibility study reports proven and probable reserves of 1,023 million tonnes at 0.453% Cu, containing 10.2 billion pounds of copper (effective 3 September 2025). Exclusive of those reserves, measured and indicated resources contain 5.4 billion pounds and inferred resources 20.0 billion pounds; each category is reported on its own.[[r:fs]]

faq.q: How long could Los Azules operate?
faq.a: The feasibility study base case is a 21-year mine life on proven and probable reserves. Beyond the study, McEwen Copper has identified two ways to process the primary sulphides, Rio Tinto's Nuton technology or a conventional concentrator, and says either could extend mine life by 30 years or more.[[r:fs]]

faq.q: What is the US$240 million term loan?
faq.a: A four-year senior secured loan at 12.0% a year that McEwen Copper closed on 27 August 2026, with Sprott Natural Resource Investment Partners (US$112 million), Rob McEwen (US$85 million) and other lenders (US$43 million). It funds engineering and early works toward the final investment decision.[[r:loan-pr]]

faq.q: How is the project being financed?
faq.a: McEwen Copper has raised US$453 million in private placements since 2021, including from Stellantis and Nuton, and closed a US$240 million term loan in August 2026. Société Générale is sole financial advisor for project debt, the IFC has signed a collaboration agreement, and the company is working toward an overall financing package of about US$4 billion.[[r:mux-la,loan-pr,sg,ifc,q2call]]

la.loan_quote: This financing reflects our lenders' confidence in Los Azules and in the progress Argentina has made over the past two and a half years. The initiatives of President Javier Milei have helped make Argentina an increasingly attractive destination for large-scale foreign investment. Economic stabilization, stronger credit ratings, lower country risk and the RIGI are bringing long-term capital back to the country. San Juan continues to demonstrate the qualities of a dependable mining jurisdiction, supported by strong institutions, rigorous processes and sound governance. We are proud to be building Los Azules here.

la.h_life: 21 years in the plan, with room for decades more
la.life_p: The feasibility study base case is a 21-year mine life on proven and probable reserves. The deposit offers more. Rio Tinto's Nuton leaching technology could allow the primary sulphides to be processed with the same infrastructure, and a conventional concentrator would lift copper recoveries and also recover gold and silver. McEwen Copper has said either route could extend mine life by 30 years or more, which could make Los Azules a mine for more than one generation.[[r:fs]]
la.life_opts: Nuton leaching or a concentrator for the primary sulphides
la.life_note: The growth case is outside the feasibility study and draws partly on inferred resources, which are too speculative geologically to have economic considerations applied to them. A concentrator would add tailings storage and water use, and either route needs further studies, permits and financing.
la.inventory_note: Each category stands on its own and the figures are not added together. Resources that are not reserves have not demonstrated economic viability.

press.bio_short: Michael Meding is Managing Director of McEwen Copper and has led the Los Azules copper project in San Juan, Argentina, since February 2022. In that time the project secured its environmental permit, completed its feasibility study, became the first copper project approved under Argentina's RIGI and closed a US$240 million term loan. He is president of GEMERA and was named Mining Entrepreneur of the Year in 2024 and 2025.
press.bio_long: Michael Meding is a German mining executive and Managing Director of McEwen Copper. Since February 2022 he has led Los Azules in San Juan, Argentina, the 10th largest undeveloped copper porphyry in the world by total mineral resources. Under his leadership the project secured its environmental permit, completed a feasibility study, became the first copper project approved under Argentina's RIGI investment regime and closed a US$240 million term loan in 2026, with Stellantis and Rio Tinto's Nuton as strategic shareholders. He came to mining from corporate finance: PwC and Novartis in Switzerland, CFO roles in Chile and Argentina, then Barrick Gold, as CFO of its Argentine operations, and Trafigura. He is president of GEMERA and vice president of CAEM, and was named Mining Entrepreneur of the Year in 2024 and 2025. He holds a BSc from Ruhr-Universität Bochum and MBAs from HHL Leipzig and Indiana University of Pennsylvania.

quotes_reference_do_not_translate.text: I’ve learned how to get things done in Argentina. Sometimes it is a matter of persistence, other times it is more about relationships than about formalities.
Me enamoré de su gente, de sus paisajes, de su cultura, de cómo ha ido creciendo con la minería.
Argentina no se va a convertir en Suiza de la noche a la mañana. Para ser exitoso en la Argentina, necesitás un buen equipo acostumbrado a manejar aguas turbulentas.
We believe in the future of Argentina. It’s in a good spot geopolitically and has what the world needs.
Queremos ser un buen vecino y que digan que somos un ejemplo de cómo se debería hacer minería.
Cuando uno quiere liderar equipos en Argentina tiene que conectarse personalmente, emocionalmente, con el personal, con los pares, para ser reconocido como un líder que la gente sigue.
Hasta diciembre del 2023, todo el mundo decía qué lástima que el proyecto está en Argentina. Hoy la respuesta es la opuesta: qué interesante que está en Argentina.
Todos mis geólogos están trabajando hoy tanto con IA como con machine learning para multiplicar sus capacidades de análisis.
Cuando trabajas en minería, te das cuenta que es absolutamente necesario el apoyo de la comunidad donde estás operando.
Nada funciona sin minería: los zapatos, el celular, el saco, el micro.
Our main challenge isn’t engineering … it’s mobilizing the necessary funding so we can move at the pace we’d like.
Es gibt in Argentinien eine große Übereinstimmung zwischen allen großen politischen Kräften. […] Das ist nicht in allen Ländern so.
Es una joya en la montaña. No solo buscaremos minimizar los impactos sino también ver qué podemos hacer para crear más biodiversidad.
La confianza se gana en gramos y se pierde en kilos.
Tenemos una oportunidad muy grande de desarrollar cuatro o cinco proyectos de gran escala en los próximos diez años.
San Juan ya juega en la Champions League, pero todavía tiene que creérsela un poco más.

quotes_tr: I fell in love with its people, its landscapes, its culture, and the way it has grown with mining.
Argentina won’t turn into Switzerland overnight. To succeed in Argentina you need a good team used to handling rough water.
We want to be a good neighbour, and for people to say we are an example of how mining should be done.
To lead teams in Argentina you have to connect personally and emotionally with your people and your peers, to be recognised as a leader people follow.
Until December 2023 everyone said what a pity the project is in Argentina. Today the answer is the opposite: how interesting that it is in Argentina.
All my geologists now work with both AI and machine learning to multiply their analytical capacity.
When you work in mining you realise that the support of the community where you operate is absolutely necessary.
Nothing works without mining: your shoes, your phone, your jacket, the bus.
In Argentina there is broad agreement among all the major political forces. […] That is not the case in every country.
It is a jewel in the mountains. We will not only seek to minimise impacts but also see what we can do to create more biodiversity.
Trust is won by the gram and lost by the kilo.
We have a very big opportunity to develop four or five large-scale projects in the next ten years.
San Juan already plays in the Champions League, but it still has to believe it a bit more.
